The issue seems to be that `RenderingDeviceDriverVulcan::texture_create_from_extension` does not set the `vk_create_info` data. This means that you cannot call `get_image()` on textures created by it.

As far as I understand it, the proper way to get the texture would be with `vkGetImageSubresourceLayout`, but this only works for linear tiling so there is a manual solution for the other case, which divides by zero. It would just work to copy the `vk_create_info`, but there is no information about the original texture info, unlike in `texture_create_shared` which is passed a `TextureID` instead of the `VkImage` directly. You also cannot simply fill in the info, because the width and height is no longer available to the driver function.


So far for the engine bugs, for your use case I think there is a workaround:

In this thread, there was the suggestion to create the texture on the main rendering device and use `texture_create_from_extension` on the local rendering device:
https://forum.godotengine.org/t/how-to-draw-texture-rid-from-local-renderingdevice-on-screen/116655/2
A
What you are doing right now is probably pretty inefficient even if it worked, because you are creating a new GPU texture every frame.

So I would put this in your `_initialize_compute_code`:
```
	var rd_main:RenderingDevice = RenderingServer.get_rendering_device()
	
	display_output_tex = Texture2DRD.new()
	display_output_tex.texture_rd_rid = rd_main.texture_create(tf, RDTextureView.new(), [])

	if texture_output_rid:
		rd.free_rid(texture_output_rid)
		
	texture_output_rid = rd.texture_create_from_extension(
		RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_TYPE_2D,
		tf.format,
		tf.samples,
		tf.usage_bits,
		rd_main.get_driver_resource(RenderingDevice.DRIVER_RESOURCE_TEXTURE, display_output_tex.texture_rd_rid, 0),
		tf.width,
		tf.height,
		tf.depth,
		tf.array_layers
	)
```
This successfully stopped the crashes in the minimal project, but I only get a black image export so there may be still something wrong with it.

@Jojo-1000's analysis is pretty close. 

The root of the problem is indeed the fact that you are created a texture extension and then attempting to retrieve its data from a different RenderingDevice. 

RenderingDevices do not share data. They are separate Vulkan devices. Its like having two different programs that work together. 

`texture_create_from_extension()` is a useful function that allows Godot to render the contents of a texture that is provided by a different application (i.e. from an OpenXR driver). 

It works by using a Vulkan API that allows sharing textures between applications, but it doesn't actually copy the memory between the applications. 

What you are doing is creating two different Vulkan devices, rendering an image in one, then reading that image in the other using the extension API. This works fine. But then you try to retrieve the image data of the extension texture from the main rendering device. Which doesn't work since the image is owned by a different rendering device. 

The solution is to stop using two different rendering devices. There is no benefit to you and you are adding workaround upon workaround to try to do something that would be easier to just do on the main renderingdevice. As a rule of thumb, you should only use a local rendering device when you explicitly do not need to share resources. Any time you need to share resources, you should be using the main rendering device. The fact that you needed to use `texture_create_from_extension()` should have been a strong indication that you were doing something wrong.

Ultimately, this shouldn't crash. In a perfect world, Godot would just error and return an empty image.

I was thinking that I should use a second rendering device because I didn't want to block on the main rendering thread, given that this is going to be called every frame.  But I can rewrite it to use the main rendering thread.
